fields.Participants: Solar Tech Support, Installation Partner, Customer
fields.Trigger: IoT monitoring detects anomaly or scheduled daily performance check

workflows.name: Solar System Remote Monitoring & Performance Alerting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-import of "import/export, inverter temperature, error codes" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews alerts daily and triages priority" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "logs service ticket in ERP" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
- operational: Solar Technical Support review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **IoT reliability**: Internet connectivity at customer sites may be intermittent; data gaps affect monitoring
- **Alert fatigue**: Minor weather-related underperformance generates excessive alerts
System Touchpoints: - IoT data ingestion API from inverter manufacturers
- Performance analytics with weather-correlation model
- Service ticket management with SLA tracking

steps.activity: IoT gateway collects real-time data from inverter: power output (kW), daily generation (kWh), grid import/export, inverter temperature, error codes; transmits to ERP via API; system compares actual vs. expected generation based on weather data (irradiance) and system specifications

System generates alerts: Underperformance (actual <80% of expected for 3 consecutive days), Inverter Error (fault code triggers diagnostic), Communication Loss (no data for 24 hours); Solar Tech Support reviews alerts daily and triages priority

For confirmed issues: Tech Support contacts customer, diagnoses remotely (inverter reset, connection check); dispatches installation partner for on-site repair if needed; logs service ticket in ERP; tracks resolution within SLA (non-critical: 5 days, critical: 2 days)

fields.Participants: Solar Tech Support, Category Manager, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Annual performance review cycle or warranty claim

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-calculate of "calculates annual degradation rate per installation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews flagged installations" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitoring data as evidence" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
- operational: Solar Technical Support review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data insufficiency**: Newer installations lack sufficient baseline data for degradation analysis
- **Vendor disputes**: Panel manufacturers may dispute warranty claims citing environmental factors
System Touchpoints: - Performance degradation analytics with weather normalization
- Warranty claim initiation with monitoring evidence attachment
- Customer communication module

steps.activity: System calculates annual degradation rate per installation: compares Year N actual generation vs. Year 1 baseline, normalized for weather (irradiance data); flags installations exceeding panel warranty degradation curve (typically <0.55%/year for Tier 1 panels)

Tech Support reviews flagged installations: determines if degradation is panel-related (manufacturing defect warrantable) vs. environmental (shading from new construction, soiling from nearby construction dust, vegetation growth)

For warrantable degradation: initiates warranty claim with panel vendor (W2544); provides monitoring data as evidence; coordinates panel testing and replacement. For environmental issues: advises customer on remediation (tree trimming, panel cleaning service)

fields.Participants: Solar Sales Coord, Vendor, Installation Partner, Finance, Customer
fields.Trigger: Customer reports solar product defect or monitoring detects performance issue

workflows.name: Solar Warranty Claim & Vendor Recovery Processing

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "Coordinator receives warranty claim" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documentation package per vendor warranty process" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-record of "record and inventory" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Long vendor processing**: Import vendor warranty claims take 4–8 weeks for resolution
- **Customer downtime**: System non-operational during warranty resolution
System Touchpoints: - Warranty claim management with multi-vendor routing
- Service dispatch for warranty inspection
- Vendor credit/replacement PO processing

steps.activity: Coordinator receives warranty claim: customer-submitted via portal or monitoring-triggered; validates warranty status (within coverage period, registered serial number); categorizes: panel defect, inverter failure, battery issue, installation workmanship

Coordinator coordinates inspection: dispatches installation partner to diagnose on-site; collects photographic evidence and test data; submits claim to vendor with documentation package per vendor warranty process (varies by manufacturer)

Upon vendor approval: Coordinator coordinates replacement delivery and installation; Finance processes vendor credit/replacement PO; system updates warranty record and inventory; if vendor rejects, escalates to Category Manager for resolution or customer accommodation

fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Solar Sales Coordinator, VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-inspect of "inspection pass rate target ≥95%" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Category Manager reviews scorecards" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
- operational: Category Manager — Electrical review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Partner scarcity**: Limited ERC-licensed solar installers in some provincial markets
- **Quality inconsistency**: Partners using subcontractors without adequate oversight
System Touchpoints: - Partner performance dashboard with automated scoring
- Inspection pass rate tracking from quality module
- Customer NPS integration from CRM

steps.activity: System generates partner scorecard: installation quality (inspection pass rate target ≥95%), schedule adherence (on-time installation target ≥90%), customer satisfaction (NPS from post-install survey), warranty claim rate (<5% within first year), safety incidents (zero tolerance)

Category Manager reviews scorecards; conducts monthly performance call with each partner; for underperformers: issues corrective action plan with 30-day improvement window; for top performers: increases lead allocation and explores volume commitments

Quarterly: Category Manager evaluates partner portfolio; onboards new partners in underserved regions (especially Visayas/Mindanao); terminates chronically underperforming partners per contract terms; maintains minimum 2 partners per region for competition

fields.Participants: CX Analyst, Category Manager, Solar Sales Coordinator

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-send of "sends automated NPS survey 30 days post-installation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "CX Analyst reviews responses" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-inspect of "inspection, performance optimization, partial refund if warranted" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low response rate**: Customers unlikely to respond to survey after completed project
- **Unrealistic expectations**: Some detractors expected higher electricity savings than system delivers
System Touchpoints: - Automated survey distribution with installation milestone trigger
- NPS analytics dashboard
- CRM feedback loop for service recovery

steps.activity: System sends automated NPS survey 30 days post-installation: product satisfaction, installation experience, communication quality, value for money, likelihood to recommend (0–10), open comments; survey completion target: >40% response rate

CX Analyst reviews responses: categorizes detractors (0–6), passives (7–8), promoters (9–10); routes detractor feedback to Category Manager for immediate follow-up within 48 hours; compiles monthly NPS report

Category Manager addresses detractor issues: coordinates service recovery (additional inspection, performance optimization, partial refund if warranted); updates training or processes based on recurring themes; reports quarterly NPS trend to VP Merchandising

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "generates solar sales dashboard" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-analyze of "Category Manager analyzes trends" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews solar category P&L" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
- operational: Category Manager — Electrical review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Revenue timing**: Installation revenue recognized over 2–8 week project cycle vs. point-of-sale
- **Margin pressure**: Solar panel prices declining globally; margin maintenance requires bundle and services focus
System Touchpoints: - BI platform with solar-specific sales analytics
- Revenue attribution for bundled product+service sales
- Category P&L reporting with margin analysis

steps.activity: BI Analyst generates solar sales dashboard: total revenue (product + installation), units sold by system size, average system price, margin by product category (panels, inverters, batteries, accessories, installation services), conversion rate (lead → sale), sales per store, regional performance

Category Manager analyzes trends: attach rate (product-only vs. product+installation), upsell rate (battery, EV charger), vendor rebate recovery, installation partner cost trends, customer segment performance (B2C vs. B2B trade); identifies top/bottom performing stores

FP&A reviews solar category P&L: revenue growth vs. forecast, gross margin (target 25–30%), customer acquisition cost, lifetime value (including cross-sell); adjusts category financial plan for next quarter

fields.Participants: Customer Service Rep, Department Supervisor, Category Manager, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Customer requests return of solar product (pre-installation) or defective unit replacement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-inspect of "inspects for physical damage" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-create of "creates vendor return authorization request" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews return trend monthly" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
- operational: Store Customer Service Rep review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **High-value returns**: Solar panel returns are PHP 8K–25K per panel; strict inspection required
- **Vendor disputes**: Vendor may reject return claiming customer damage
System Touchpoints: - Return processing with vendor RMA integration
- Inventory quarantine management
- Return analytics dashboard

steps.activity: Customer Service Rep processes return request: verifies purchase within 30-day return window (standard) or warranty period (defective); for panels/inverters — inspects for physical damage; for special-order items — confirms return authorization per vendor policy

Supervisor approves return; system processes refund (cash/card reversal) or exchange; for defective items: creates vendor return authorization request; items placed in defective quarantine area; customer receives replacement from stock or special order

Category Manager reviews return trend monthly: high return rate SKUs flagged for quality review with vendor; defective analysis by vendor, product type, and batch/lot; adjusts inventory buffers for high-return SKUs

fields.Participants: Category Mgr, Procurement, Legal, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Monthly intelligence cycle or regulatory announcement

workflows.name: Solar Market Intelligence & Regulatory Update Monitoring

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitors market developments" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews regulatory changes" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "Category Manager incorporates intelligence into strategy" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-441 (ensure controlled execution — Solar After-Sales Monitoring & Analytics (PA-70.3).)
- operational: Category Manager — Electrical review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Regulatory uncertainty**: Philippine renewable energy policy subject to frequent changes
- **Global supply volatility**: Solar panel prices affected by Chinese trade policy and raw material costs
System Touchpoints: - Market intelligence repository
- Regulatory change log with compliance tracking
- Pricing engine updates for tax treatment changes

steps.activity: Category Manager monitors market developments: global solar panel pricing trends (spot market), Philippine ERC net metering policy changes, DU-specific interconnection rule updates, government solar incentive programs (BOI tax holidays for solar manufacturers), competitor solar pricing and assortment

Legal reviews regulatory changes: ERC circulars, DOE renewable energy targets, LGU building code amendments affecting solar installations, BIR tax treatment of solar sales (VAT zero-rating for renewable energy equipment per RA 9513); updates compliance requirements

Category Manager incorporates intelligence into strategy: adjusts pricing based on global panel cost trends, updates assortment for new technology (e.g., bifacial panels, solid-state batteries), modifies sales approach for regulatory changes, briefs Store Ops and Training on updates
